baseline_models.focus_anchor: The conditional sequence from yadhharu alaykum to yarjumukum aw yuidukum.
baseline_models.mechanism: Appearance over the youths carries both discovery and ascendancy: concealment fails, control is gained, and control forks into punitive elimination or forced reversal.

activation_trace.role: Finding what was hidden supplies the exposure event that opens the conditional.
Ascendancy over another supplies the capture and mastery threshold in alaykum.
The stone cluster supplies the concrete material endpoint of the punitive alternative.
Return after departure supplies the coercive reversal in the second alternative.

changed_reading.before: A generic warning that discovery will bring punishment or conversion.
changed_reading.after: A breach-to-control cascade: detection becomes mastery and then forks into bodily elimination or forced reversal.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Yuidukum fi millatihim followed by lan tuflihu idhan abada.
baseline_models.mechanism: Causative return into a milla is not mere relocation. The enclosing fi, return, habit, followed creed, and worn path form a mechanism of re-habituation; its terminal cost is loss of enduring good without a future exit.

activation_trace.role: Habit acquired through repeated practice supplies the disciplinary depth of forced return.
A followed creed supplies the normative system into which the youths would be reinserted.
A road worn by repeated passage supplies the patterned track that coercion would make them walk again.
Winning, survival, and lasting good define what forced reinsertion would foreclose.
Unbounded duration turns the loss from a temporary setback into an irreversible horizon.

changed_reading.before: They may be made to profess the townspeople's religion again and consequently fail.
changed_reading.after: They may be reconditioned into a practiced social-religious track whose success is precisely the permanent erasure of their achieved departure.

context_deltas.mechanism: Counted years, a measured stay, and awakening from stillness make the focus ayah's abada contrast bounded suspension with irreversible loss: sleep can end, but coerced return would close the horizon of flourishing.

activation_trace.role: Perpetual duration supplies the unbounded side of the temporal contrast.
Counting makes the long sleep determinate rather than endless.
Stirring the still from rest supplies a real exit from prolonged suspension.
Tarrying in a place supplies the bounded state whose duration is assessed.
An endpoint supplies a limit against which abada becomes sharply unlimited.

structural_cues: The sequence moves from numbered years in 18:11 to awakening and measurement in 18:12, then to the unbounded consequence in 18:20.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies counted stasis, an awakening, and an endpoint; I infer a contrast between reversible suspension and irreversible coerced return. A live alternative is that abada is emphatic idiom without a deliberate contrast to the measured sleep.

changed_reading.before: Never succeeding is an emphatic extension of the warning.
changed_reading.after: Never succeeding is the unbounded counterterm to their bounded sleep: divine suspension returns them to agency, while coerced return would end that agency permanently.

context_deltas.mechanism: The youths' departure has an inner, public, and social sequence: hearts are fastened, they stand and declare, then withdraw from the people's worship. Forced return would run that whole sequence backward, not merely alter a label.

activation_trace.role: Return after departure supplies the reversal of an already completed exit.
The followed creed supplies the social-religious order to which they would be restored.
Fastening the heart supplies the inner stabilization that coercion would have to undo.
Rising with resolve supplies the public enactment of their separation.
Withdrawal to a side supplies the social and spatial completion of departure.
Submissive worship identifies the practice from which the withdrawal is made.

structural_cues: Across 18:14-16, inner fastening precedes public standing and physical withdrawal into refuge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a staged exit of heart, speech, worship, and location; I infer that the captors' causative return reverses each layer. A live alternative is coerced outward conformity while inward conviction survives.

changed_reading.before: The captors would convert the youths back.
changed_reading.after: The captors would dismantle a hard-won, multi-layered secession and reinsert the youths into the very practice and social track they deliberately left.

context_deltas.mechanism: Silver must cross into the city through one discreet agent who must prevent any awareness of the group. The focus conditional is therefore the named failure state of a covert provisioning operation: traceable exchange exposes identity, exposure yields control, and control activates the coercive fork.

activation_trace.role: Discovery supplies the information breach feared at the end of the mission.
Mastery supplies the immediate escalation from being identified to being captured.
Silver money supplies the observable token that must enter circulation.
The gathered city supplies the dense social field in which the token and agent can be recognized.
Fineness and hiddenness supply the required low-visibility mode of conduct.
Fine-grained awareness supplies the perception that must not be triggered in anyone.

structural_cues: The mission imperatives in 18:19 culminate in preventing awareness, and 18:20 immediately gives the causal consequence if that prevention fails.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies money, city entry, subtle conduct, suppressed awareness, and then the discovery conditional; I infer an operational leak-to-capture arrow. A live alternative is that the transaction details are only narrative setting and discovery could arise by another route.

changed_reading.before: If townspeople happen to find the youths, persecution follows.
changed_reading.after: The warning is an operational threat model: a necessary market transaction can leak identity, turn social perception into capture, and expose the whole group to elimination or reconditioning.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah causes the hidden youths to be found so that others know a promise is true. Discovery is thus not intrinsically defeat: enemy-timed discovery activates coercion, while divinely timed disclosure converts the same vulnerability into public evidence.

activation_trace.role: Finding the concealed group supplies the threatened event whose agency and purpose are revised.
Coming upon what was hidden supplies the purposeful disclosure immediately after the warning.
Knowledge as disclosure supplies the public cognitive result of their being found.
A promise that opens hope supplies the proposition their disclosure is made to confirm.
Truth fixed to reality supplies the evidentiary status produced by the disclosure.

structural_cues: The feared if-they-find-you construction in 18:20 is immediately followed by thus-We-caused-them-to-be-found and a purpose clause in 18:21.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two discoveries with different agents and an explicit knowledge-purpose for the second; I infer that timing, agency, and purpose determine whether exposure destroys agency or bears witness. A live alternative is that 18:21 occurs only after the original danger has expired and therefore does not revise the warning itself.

changed_reading.before: Discovery is the terminal failure of concealment.
changed_reading.after: Premature hostile discovery is failure, but disclosure itself can be providentially retimed: the once-dangerous visibility becomes the means by which concealed truth is made knowable.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because yarjumukum in 18:20 points first to bodily stoning. It remains anchored because 18:22 repeats the same root for conjectural casting about the unseen and the focus inventory also carries injurious speech; downstream prose should retain physical execution as primary and present discursive stoning only as a secondary afterlife of exposure.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Yarjumukum in 18:20, revisited by rajman bil-ghayb in 18:22.

activation_trace.role: The stone cluster preserves the primary bodily and material force of the threat.
Injurious speech figured as stone-throwing opens a secondary social mode without replacing the literal threat.
Casting conjecture into the unseen supplies the later verbal recurrence of the focus root.
Concealment from sight supplies the epistemic absence into which later speakers cast their claims.

changed_reading.before: Exposure leaves the youths vulnerable to execution by stones.
changed_reading.after: Exposure has a contained double vulnerability: bodies can be stoned under hostile power, while the absent or hidden group can later be pelted with ungrounded public conjecture.

strongest_changes: The immediate 18:19 sequence turns 18:20 into a concrete leak-to-capture threat model rather than a generic warning.
The staged secession of 18:14-16 makes return to the milla a reversal of inner, public, ritual, and spatial agency.
The purposeful finding in 18:21 reverses discovery from intrinsic defeat into an event whose value depends on agent, timing, and purpose.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah compresses information exposure, coercive branching, social re-habituation, and permanent consequence, while the next ayah immediately transforms feared visibility into evidence.
remaining_uncertainties: Yadhharu alaykum may foreground discovery, dominance, or a rapid transition between both.
Forced return may denote outward compliance, inward re-habituation, or both.
The conjectural r-j-m layer is packet-licensed but should not displace the primary bodily threat.
